disposition_reason: The paper states that the chicken meat and egg contents in Tables 1 and 2 are those obtained by Acho et al. (2019, ref. 5), the authors' earlier study; the 2026 paper adds a food-frequency survey and a dietary risk assessment on those reprinted values. To count the data once, no findings are recorded from this reprint.
disposition_locator: Section 4.2, p. 726 ('The contents of chicken meat and eggs obtained by ACHO et al (2019) [5] are recorded in tables 1 and 2'); Tables 1-2

study.design: dietary risk assessment built on previously published occurrence data plus a food-frequency survey (Yopougon, Cocody, Marcory)
study.origin: hen farms in Agnibilekrou (3 farms) and Abidjan near kilometre 17, Yopougon (2 farms), Cote d'Ivoire
study.method: graphite-furnace AAS (Varian SpectrAA 110); meat by microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion, eggs by dry ashing at 500 C
study.qa: blank and two series of calibration standards; no CRM or recovery reported

unresolved: Tables 1-2 reprint Acho et al. 2019 ('Level of contamination by heavy metals (lead and cadmium) in products from poultry farms in Cote d'Ivoire'); that primary paper is not in the corpus and was not available here, so the occurrence values are not recorded as findings.

Reprinted values for reference only: chicken meat Abidjan Pb 0.067 +/- 20, Cd 0.302 +/- 30; Agnibilekrou Pb 0.060 +/- 30, Cd 0.089 +/- 70 mg/kg (SD cells implausible as printed). Eggs Abidjan Pb 0.067 +/- 0.02, Cd 25.96 +/- 15.24; Agnibilekrou Pb 0.35 +/- 0.09, Cd 35.46 +/- 14.04 ug/kg.
Table 4 uses different concentrations from Tables 1-2 (chicken meat Pb 63 and Cd 174.6 ug/kg; eggs Pb 0.16 and Cd 29.13 ug/kg) without explanation.
The text calls the meat 'guinea fowl meat' in Section 4.2 while the tables and methods describe hen (Gallus gallus) meat.
